reconcile.note: Gill harmonizes the two death-sites by identifying Mosera as the name of the desert surrounding Mount Hor, so both accounts describe the same location.

discrepancy.note: Colenso documents that Deuteronomy's Mosera death-notice for Aaron directly conflicts with Numbers' account of his death atop Mount Hor.

quotes.text: Aaron died at Mosera; whereas in N.xxxiii.31-38 we read that they marched from Moseroth to Bene-jaakan … and thence proceed to Moimt Hor, where Aaron died.
quotes.attr: John William Colenso (d. 1883), The Pentateuch and Book of Joshua Critically Examined, Part I (1862), on Deuteronomy 10:6 and Numbers 20:28.

sides.snippet: Moses stripped Aaron of his garments, and put them on Eleazar his son; and Aaron died there on the top of the mountain: and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
sides.verseText: Moses stripped Aaron of his garments, and put them on Eleazar his son; and Aaron died there on the top of the mountain: and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.

sides.snippet: (The children of Israel traveled from Beeroth Bene Jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died, and there he was buried; and Eleazar his son ministered in the priest's office in his place.
